Available in cPanel 66 and later. This function activates PHP-FPM for any non-PHP-FPM domains on a server.

**Important:**

When you disable the [*Web Server*](https://go.cpanel.net/howtouseserverprofiles) role, the system **disables** this function.

**Warning:**

We **strongly** recommend that you only activate Apache PHP-FPM if your server has at least 2 GB of RAM available, or at least 30 MB of RAM per domain. If you enable PHP-FPM on a server with less than the required RAM, your server may experience severe performance issues.

Converts existing non-PHP-FPM domains server-wide. The returned build_id identifies a log file, not successful completion or application availability. Configuration can change immediately; no retry or rollback is provided.

Available in cPanel 64 and later. This function creates an EasyApache 4 profile. This function only writes files to the `/etc/cpanel/ea4/profiles/custom/` directory.

**Important**:

  When you disable the [Web Server role](https://go.cpanel.net/serverroles), the system **disables** this function.

Writes only /etc/cpanel/ea4/profiles/custom/. filename, display name and packages are required; optional desc defaults to empty string, overwrite to 0, tags to an empty list and version to the string 0. Overwriting can replace an existing profile. already_exists is returned only for an existing filename with overwrite=0; path only on success.

An explicit empty tags list omits the optional tag field, matching its pinned empty default. Nonempty tag/package lists retain repeated-key encoding; required packages and all other list inputs keep existing validation. Explicit false overwrite is sent as 0. Each request is form-encoded once with no retry or rollback.

Available in cPanel 11.52 and later. This function changes the contents of a PHP version's php.ini file.

**Notes:**

 - This document **only** applies to systems that run EasyApache 4.
 - Due to the limited field length of HTTP GET method calls, we **strongly** recommend that you use the HTTP POST method.

**Important:**
  When you disable the [Web Server role](https://go.cpanel.net/serverroles), the system **disables** this function.

content is sensitive caller-supplied text. The client form-encodes its exact bytes once; callers do not pre-encode them. This replaces the selected version's php.ini contents and can affect sites using it immediately. No retry or rollback is provided, and no server write/read round trip is established by offline coverage.

The PR 58 PHP.pm source report places this write in the return {} family. A successful absent or null data member returns null; any present non-null payload retains its existing contract. This is source-only compatibility, unobserved for this POST.

Available in cPanel 66 and later. This function determines whether to enable PHP-FPM on new accounts and domains on a server.

**Important:**

When you disable the [Web Server role](https://docs.cpanel.net/knowledge-base/general-systems-administration/how-to-use-server-profiles/#roles), the system **disables** this function.

**Warning:**

We **strongly** recommend that you only activate Apache PHP-FPM if your server has at least 2 GB of RAM available, or at least 30 MB of RAM per domain. If you enable PHP-FPM on a server with less than the required RAM, your server may experience severe performance issues.

This changes the default for new accounts and domains; it does not convert existing domains. Use convertAllDomainsToFpm separately to activate existing non-FPM domains. The pinned source data schema is unconstrained.
